1.title: Route des Vins d'Alsace: The Wine Road Through the Region
1.html:
The Alsace Wine Route (Route des Vins d'Alsace) winds along the gentle vineyard slopes on the eastern foot of the Vosges, from Marlenheim (west of Strasbourg) in the north to Thann (northwest of Mulhouse) in the south, running through the whole long narrow belt of the Alsace wine region and linking hundreds of wine villages along the way.

The whole route broadly follows the geographical logic of the vineyards, passing through core wine towns such as Molsheim → Obernai → Barr → Ribeauvillé → Riquewihr → Colmar → Eguisheim → Guebwiller → Thann, and is one of the oldest and most famous wine tourism routes in all France.
2.title: Bas-Rhin and Haut-Rhin: Two Worlds in Two Départements
2.html:
The Alsace wine region administratively spans two départements, the boundary lying around Sélestat (Colmar is the capital of Haut-Rhin in the south):

  • Bas-Rhin (Lower Rhine, the northern section): covers the Strasbourg, Molsheim, Obernai and Barr area — the Vosges are relatively low here and give the vineyards weaker rain-shadow protection, so the climate is slightly cooler
  • Haut-Rhin (Upper Rhine, the southern section): covers the Ribeauvillé, Riquewihr, Colmar, Eguisheim and Guebwiller area — the Vosges are at their highest here with the strongest rain-shadow effect, making it the core heartland of Alsace wine, and the great majority of the 51 Grand Crus lie here
3.title: Half-Timbered Fairy-Tale Villages: Not Just Wine, but Living Cultural Heritage
3.html:
Along the wine road, a series of well-preserved villages of half-timbered buildings (colombage) make up the unique visual image of Alsace — colourful timber-framed houses, cobbled streets and church spires make the villages themselves living cultural heritage:

  • Riquewihr: praised as one of the "most beautiful villages of France", its walls and timber-framed old street almost completely preserved from the Middle Ages
  • Eguisheim: famous for its concentric streets, and the legendary birthplace of Pope Léon IX
  • Kaysersberg: the birthplace of Albert Schweitzer, voted "the French people's favourite village" in 2017
  • Ribeauvillé, Colmar: important towns of the southern stretch of the wine road, and Colmar is also known for its "Little Venice" (Petite Venise) canal quarter

In the Christmas season many villages turn into famous Christmas markets (Marché de Noël); Colmar, Ribeauvillé and Riquewihr are all representative towns of Alsace's Christmas market culture, closely interweaving wine tourism and festive culture.
4.question: What is the geographical extent of the Route des Vins d'Alsace (Alsace Wine Route)?
4.options.0: Limited to the area around the city of Colmar
4.options.1: From Marlenheim in the north to Thann in the south, running through the whole long narrow Alsace region
4.options.3: Stretching from the German border to the Swiss border
4.explanation: The Alsace Wine Route runs from Marlenheim, west of Strasbourg, in the north to Thann, northwest of Mulhouse, in the south, winding along the eastern foot of the Vosges through the whole long narrow belt of the Alsace wine region and passing hundreds of wine villages, one of the oldest wine tourism routes in all France.
